top_choice_rationale: P004 credits a principle of molecular organisation: liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent biomolecules, shown in P-granule liquid behaviour (Brangwynne, Hyman) and in reconstituted systems with a quantitative phase boundary set by valency and affinity (Rosen). It is thermodynamics applied to biomolecules and was tested independently. I accept that Pappu and Mittag are left out and that in vivo claims are contested, so the citation should be limited to the physical-chemical principle. P001 is my second choice: B023 has the cleanest attribution and B060 is a distinct chemical outcome from Cas9 cleavage. P002 follows because perovskites are structurally well characterised, then P003, which has an unresolved cereblon and molecular-glue scope and no approved degrader. A prize is still better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my field is close to condensates and soft-matter self-assembly, but my profile lists no personal, institutional, mentor or collaborator tie to Hyman, Brangwynne or Rosen.
